Methodology

Original range is the EPA combined range for the exact model year / model / trim from fueleconomy.gov (each car's report links the specific EPA record). Where EPA rates wheel options separately, the base wheel rating is used and noted.

Staff confirmations. Each report's Confirm details button opens the car's row in the shared Google Sheet. When staff record an actual full-charge range (range shown at 100%) or a battery-health % from a Tesla test, the app shows ACTUAL health (actual range ÷ original EPA range, or the entered %) and uses it for the color band and sorting; the estimate stays visible for comparison. Confirmed hardware replaces the estimate. Confirmations last synced: 2026-10-10T14:23:20.

Estimated battery health (state of health, SoH):

SoH = 100 − A·(1 − e−miles/25,000) − B·(miles/1,000) − C·(age in years) − performance penalty

  • Early "break-in" loss (A): batteries lose capacity fastest in the first ~10–50k miles, then level off (Recurrent; Tesla Impact Report curve). A = 7 pts max.
  • Slow linear cycling loss (B): 0.035 pts per 1,000 mi for NCA/NMC packs, 0.025 for LFP packs (LFP has higher cycle life).
  • Calendar aging (C): 0.8 pts/yr for NCA/NMC, 0.6 pts/yr for LFP. Age is measured from Jan 1 of the model year.
  • Performance/Plaid penalty: −2 pts (Tesla-reported CPO data shows Performance trims ~1–3 pts below Long Range at similar mileage).
  • Estimated current range = original EPA range × SoH. Difference = estimated current range − original EPA range.

Calibration. Sources disagree, so the curve is set between them: Tesla's own fleet average is the optimistic end (Model 3/Y Long Range keep ~85% after 200,000 mi; Model S/X ~88%), and Tesla-reported health on used Certified Pre-Owned listings (compiled by ev-inventory.com) is the cautious end (e.g. 2018–19 Model 3 LR AWD ≈ 83% at ~69k mi; 2021–23 Model 3 RWD (LFP) ≈ 91.5% at ~36k mi; Model Y LR AWD ≈ 88% at ~42k mi; Model Y Performance ≈ 85% at ~42k mi; Model S Plaid ≈ 85.6% at ~53k mi). Recurrent's data falls in between: Model 3 keeps ~95% of range at 3 years and ~93% at 5, Model Y ~96% / 95%, with 1–2% loss per year that is fastest in the first 50k miles. With these settings the model gives ~88–89% at 40k mi / 4.5 yrs, ~85–86% at 70k mi / 7 yrs and ~80% at 200k mi / 7 yrs.

Not included (they can move real health several points either way): climate (sustained Florida heat speeds up aging), how often the car was fast-charged or kept at 100%, pack replacements under warranty, and Tesla software range changes. Tesla's battery warranty covers 8 yrs / 100k mi (Standard Range) or 8 yrs / 120k mi (Long Range/Performance) down to 70% capacity.

Computer & software

Autopilot computer and infotainment computer are estimated from the VIN (digit 10 model year, digit 11 plant, digits 12–17 production sequence) plus model/trim, using published transition points: Model 3 kept HW3 until the 2024 "Highland" refresh; Model Y switched to HW4 at Fremont from VIN sequence ~789500 (May 24 2023) and at Austin from ~131200 (Jun 4 2023); Model S/X switched ~Feb–Mar 2023 (2021–22 Plaid = HW3 + AMD Ryzen). The AMD Ryzen (MCU3) infotainment computer replaced the Intel Atom (MCU2) on US Model 3/Y from late Dec 2021 (first Model 3 VIN ~139xxx, Model Y ~356xxx) with mixed builds until end of Q2 2022. A * in the table means medium/low confidence and ✓ means confirmed by staff in the confirmations sheet (confirmed values override estimates): confirm on the car under Controls > Software > Additional Vehicle Information. Latest software versions checked 2026-10-10 (current: 2026.38.3.1); FSD applies only to cars with FSD purchased or subscribed.

  • r/TeslaModelY AP04 (HW4) VIN tracker – Fremont PF789500+, Austin PA131200+ (May/Jun 2023)
  • Tesla Model Y service manual – VIN decoding (digit 10 model year, digit 11 plant, 12-17 sequence)
  • TSLNA – HW3 vs HW4 timeline (Model 3 HW4 only with 2024 Highland; S/X HW4 ~Feb–Mar 2023)
  • Teslarati – first North American Model 3/Y with AMD Ryzen MCU3 (built Dec 21 2021, Model 3 VIN 139xxx)
  • TMC – 2022 Model Y Ryzen transition (VIN ~356xxx+, Jan 2022; full switch by end Q2 2022)
  • Carnex – Tesla hardware/MCU generations (MCU2 Intel Atom 2018–2021, Ryzen S/X 2021+)
  • Not a Tesla App – software updates (TeslaFi fleet stats)
  • Not a Tesla App – 2026.33.5 (FSD 14.3.11) release notes

  • Tesla Oracle – FSD v14.3.11 (2026.33.5) rollout (Oct 8, 2026)

Suggested retail (market pricing)

Every suggested price is computed only from real used-Tesla listings found for sale (comps last collected 2026-10-09); each report lists the exact comps used with price, miles, year, trim, color, location, source and a link to the listing. No price is invented: only comps within 500 miles of Lux's lot are used (comps farther away or with an unknown location are excluded, and the search is never widened beyond 500 mi); if fewer than 3 such comps match, the car shows Insufficient data — few comps within 500 mi.

  • Distance: every comp must be within 500 mi (straight line) of Lux, 705 W Memorial Blvd, Lakeland FL — from the dealer's address coordinates, else its ZIP centroid, else its city centroid (GeoNames), else the listing site's own distance from Lakeland; comps with no usable location are dropped. This applies to suggested retail, the range, confidence, comp cards and the Demand score.
  • Matching: same model, same model year, same trim group (Standard/Long Range/Performance/Plaid) and same drivetrain; mileage within ±35% (min ±20k mi) of the car, nearest first (up to 12). If fewer than 5 match, the mileage band widens to ±70% (min ±40k), then adjacent model years are allowed (confidence drops). Same estimated Autopilot computer (HW3 vs HW4, decoded from each comp's VIN) is required when at least 5 such comps exist. Same exterior color is a small tie-breaker only.
  • Mileage adjustment: the $/mile slope is fitted on the selected comps (Theil–Sen: median of all pairwise price/mile slopes, robust to outliers); each comp's price is moved to this car's odometer. Suggested retail = median of the adjusted prices, weighted so comps closer in mileage count more (weight = 1 / (1 + (mile difference ÷ 15,000)²)); range = weighted 25th–75th percentile. Rounded to $100. Lux's own cars (also listed on Autotrader) are excluded from comps.
  • Battery: estimated health is a function of miles and age, which the mileage adjustment already prices, so no extra adjustment is made for estimates. When staff record an ACTUAL health in the confirmations sheet, the price moves ±0.5% per point of difference from the estimate (capped at ±5%).
  • Confidence: High = ≥8 same-year comps and an IQR under 12% of the price; Medium = ≥5 same-year comps; Low = adjacent years needed, only 3–4 comps, comps mostly listed with a drivetrain-only trim, or comps far from this car's mileage (Medium if moderately far); Insufficient data = fewer than 3 comps within 500 mi. 3–4 comps are flagged “Few comps within 500 mi”.
  • vs Market = Lux listed website price − suggested retail (the website price excludes the dealer fee). Below/above range means the listed price is outside the comps' 25th–75th percentile band.
  • Comp card order (display only, does not change the price): cards are ranked by a match score = 0.5 × distance from Lux's lot (705 W Memorial Blvd, Lakeland, FL 33815) ÷ the farthest comp's distance + 0.5 × mileage gap ÷ the largest gap, minus 0.15 for the same exterior color, 0.15 for the same interior color and 0.10 extra when both match; ties go to the closest car. Distance is straight-line miles from the dealer's address coordinates (Autotrader) or the dealer ZIP centroid (GeoNames). Colors are compared by basic color family; "interior unknown" means the listing didn't give one. Use the Best match / Closest / Price / Mileage buttons to re-order.
  • Manheim MMR is shown for reference only (never used in the suggested retail). Values come from Manheim pulls by VIN (mmr.json) when available, otherwise from staff entries in the Confirm details sheet (columns U–X); nothing is estimated.
  • Region: comps come from Autotrader's 500-mile search around Lakeland, FL (sorted by distance) plus Autotrader/Cars.com wider searches, then are cut to 500 mi from Lux, so they are Florida/Southeast listings. Each report shows how many comps are in Florida. Comps are asking prices, not sold prices.

Views: ALL / TESLAS / ICE / GAS / DIESEL

The switch at the top filters the same inventory; counts show the vehicles currently shown (available only unless Show sold vehicles is ticked — SOLD vehicles are hidden by default). TESLAS is the original battery report (unchanged columns and ratings). ICE = gasoline and diesel vehicles (no battery data); GAS = gasoline only (incl. flex-fuel); DIESEL = diesel only. TRUCKS / SUVS / SEDANS = body style, Teslas and ICE together (ALL columns): from the NHTSA VIN decode's body class, else the dealer listing's body/title (Tesla Model 3/S = sedan, Model Y/X = SUV, Cybertruck = truck). Coupes, convertibles, vans and wagons are in none of the three but still appear under ALL. Any non-Tesla EV or hybrid would get its own tag and appear under ALL (none are in stock today). Inventory, photos, price, colors, engine, transmission, drivetrain, fuel and body come from the dealer website's own inventory feed (78 vehicles captured = the site's own total of 78: 27 Teslas, 51 ICE).

ICE pricing (same method as Teslas)

  • Matching: Autotrader listings of the same make/model code and model year (adjacent years only if thin), same fuel (diesel vs gasoline), same drivetrain family when ≥3 such comps exist (Autotrader groups AWD and 4WD together), and same trim name when ≥3 comps share it (otherwise mixed trims are used and confidence is capped at Medium). Cab/bed length is not filtered (not consistently stated in listings). Mileage weighting, Theil–Sen mileage adjustment, ranges, confidence rules, comp-card order and Lux's own cars being excluded are identical to the Tesla method.

Demand score (how hot the vehicle is)

Built only from real market data for the same-spec comparable listings within 500 mi (same pool as pricing, before the mileage cut), Lux's own listings excluded. Each available input gives a 0–100 sub-score; the Demand score is their average:

  • Days on market — median Autotrader "days on site" of the comps: ≤30 days = 100, ≥120 days = 0, linear in between.
  • Price cuts — share of comps that show a price reduction (Autotrader's reduced-price flag or a drop in its price history): 0% = 100, ≥60% = 0.
  • Manheim transactions — only when the vehicle's MMR has been pulled: ≥50 transactions = 100, ≤5 = 0 (log scale). Shown as "MMR pending" until then.
  • Context, not scored: number of same-spec listings found within 500 mi, how many are within 250 mi of Lux, Autotrader's nationwide count for the same year/model (all trims), and where comps sit vs Kelley Blue Book fair price. Supply is not scored because no sales-volume denominator is available for every model.

Hot ≥65 (green) · Warm 40–64 (orange) · Cool <40 (red). Confidence: High = ≥15 comps with days-on-market data plus Manheim transactions; Medium = ≥8 comps; Low = 3–7 comps; fewer than 3 = "Insufficient data" (no label). Teslas show the same Demand line inside their report, alongside — not instead of — the battery rating.

ICE vehicle data

  • VIN decode: NHTSA vPIC (vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov/api).
  • Recalls: NHTSA recalls API by make/model/year (api.nhtsa.gov). These are campaigns for the model/year, not proof the VIN is affected or still open — use each report's link to check the VIN on nhtsa.gov/recalls. Owner complaint counts come from the NHTSA complaints API (reports, not verified defects).
  • Fuel economy: EPA combined/city/highway mpg from fueleconomy.gov web services, matched to year/make/model/engine/drive; a few configurations were matched by hand. Heavy-duty pickups over 8,500 lb GVWR are not EPA-rated; vehicles without a confident match show n/a.
  • Mileage vs typical (informational only): odometer ÷ age vs ~13,500 mi/yr (FHWA average per driver), age from Jan 1 of the model year.
  • Warranty (estimate): manufacturers' published new-vehicle terms for the model year — e.g. Ford/Chevrolet/GMC/RAM/Jeep/Chrysler/Honda/Toyota/Nissan 3 yr/36k basic + 5 yr/60k powertrain; Ford Power Stroke, GM Duramax and RAM Cummins diesel engines 5 yr/100k; Lexus 4/50k + 6/70k; Hyundai 5/60k (10/100k powertrain for original owners only); Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Audi, Porsche, Volvo, Land Rover 4 yr/50k; VW 2018–19 Tiguan 6 yr/72k, later 4 yr/50k. In-service date assumed Jan 1 of the model year; verify against CARFAX.
  • MSRP and "common issues" are not shown: no source of real per-VIN MSRP or reputable common-issue data was used, so nothing is guessed.

CARFAX

Badges come from each vehicle's CARFAX report pulled by Lux (owners, accidents/damage with severity as CARFAX states it, structural/title/odometer/total-loss flags, rental/fleet use, service records, CARFAX value and warranty line). Colors: green = 1-Owner / No Accidents; neutral = 2 owners, personal/lease use, reliability and service badges; orange = 3+ owners, minor damage, accident with severity not stated, any rental/fleet/corporate/commercial history; red = Open Recall (CARFAX "At Least 1 Open Recall"), major/severe or structural damage, total loss, title or odometer issue. The "Any damage" filter counts any reported accident or red damage flag (an open recall alone is not damage). "Show full CARFAX" embeds the PDF snapshot (on phones use the "Open full CARFAX (PDF)" button); the live CARFAX link works only for logged-in dealer accounts. Vehicles without a report show "CARFAX pending".
